read.thesis: Schwab delivered record 2025 (adj EPS $4.87, +50%) and guides 2026 EPS $5.70-5.80 on 9.5-10.5% revenue growth, with ~5% organic asset growth and no buybacks assumed in the scenario.

triggers.label: 2026 adj EPS $5.70-5.80
triggers.quote: this full year scenario implies potential adjusted earnings of around the $5.70 to $5.80 range, which would represent year-over-year earnings growth in the upper teens.

triggers.label: Core NNA $519bn, +42%
triggers.quote: We attracted $519 billion in core net new assets or NNA, a 42% increase over last year.

triggers.label: 2026 expense growth 5.5-6.5%
triggers.quote: we anticipate annual expense growth to range from 5.5% to 6.5%.

triggers.label: Trading volume slight pullback assumed
triggers.quote: our 2026 scenario does allow for a slight pullback in volumes to roughly 7.4 million daily average trades for the full year.

guidance.quote: we would expect total revenue growth of 9.5% to 10.5% in 2026.
full year organic asset growth of around 5%.
Full year net interest margin expands to a range of 2.85% to 2.95%
we anticipate annual expense growth to range from 5.5% to 6.5%.
this full year scenario implies potential adjusted earnings of around the $5.70 to $5.80 range
that is still our objective. And keep in mind

red_flags.label: Trading volume normalisation assumed
red_flags.quote: our 2026 scenario does allow for a slight pullback in volumes to roughly 7.4 million daily average trades

evasions.quote: what we provided in that scenario and the implied math does not include buybacks.
there is no arbitrary target on that or ceiling on that per se.
